dropped.1: additive: CreatePostgresDbOptions gains optional connectTimeoutSeconds and queryTimeoutMs (network-partition query bound); backward-compatible, and aai-runtime has no external consumer to keep an epoch-1 template for
dropped.2: Epoch 2 promised SweepSkip, which the surface no longer exports — and epoch 4 was dropped for exactly that removal. It read as supported only because its frozen example never named the type, so the retain was a claim nothing could have detected: a consumer naming SweepSkip has not compiled since it went. Dropped rather than narrowed, because aai-runtime has no external consumer to keep an epoch-2 template for.
dropped.3: The Db type moved from the aai root to @alexkroman1/aai/internal when ctx.db was removed — it is no longer an authoring type, only the shape this runtime's own Postgres consumers take. Nothing about the names or signatures changed, so a host using createPostgresDb is unaffected; a host that hand-wrote a Db and imported the type from the root must change the specifier.
dropped.4: SweepSkip is REMOVED. It described what the graphile-worker lock sweep reports when it declines, and that sweep went with the Workflow DevKit — there is no mechanism left for the name to describe. A consumer naming the type no longer compiles, which is what makes this a drop rather than a retain.

dropped.1: The eval workflow engine's WorkflowCtx gained sleep (recorded, not taken) and waitFor (refused with a named message, a hook's payload coming from outside the run). Its types also moved to workflow-engine-types.ts under the 500-line cap, which the rollup's provenance shows.
dropped.2: EvalSleep carries the wait's label, so a workflow eval can assert which of a body's waits it reached rather than only a duration.
dropped.3: Renamed for naming consistency (API naming review): this epoch's frozen example uses a name the rename removed, so the promise it encoded is withdrawn. See the reason on the epoch dropped alongside it. Epoch 3's example uses the Fake* speech doubles, now Stub*.
dropped.4: Renamed for naming consistency (API naming review): the eval speech doubles joined the repo's single Stub vocabulary (FakeSpeech -> StubSpeechProviders and family), since Fake vs Stub carried no meaning while the shared word Speech did. callsIn and toolCallsIn, which differed only in what they took, became toolCallsInTurns and toolCallsInEvents.

dropped.3: Renamed for naming consistency (API naming review): this epoch's frozen example uses a name the rename removed, so the promise it encoded is withdrawn. See the reason on the epoch dropped alongside it. Epoch 3's example uses decliningRuntime, now rejectingRuntime.
dropped.4: Renamed for naming consistency (API naming review): this epoch's frozen example uses a name the rename removed, so the promise it encoded is withdrawn. See the reason on the epoch dropped alongside it. Epoch 4's example uses SkipGreeting, now SkipGreetingOption.
dropped.5: `WorkflowCtx.step`'s `name` narrowed from `string` to `Name & Literal<Name>`, so a name that has widened to `string` — exactly the shape that re-executes a step on replay — is now a compile error rather than a runtime surprise. Epoch N authoring code that built a step name at runtime therefore does not compile, which is the point of the change; and this package has no external consumer to keep an epoch-N template for.
dropped.6: Renamed for naming consistency (API naming review): this epoch's export list promises decliningRuntime and SkipGreeting, both of which the rename removed (now rejectingRuntime and SkipGreetingOption). Source written at epoch 6 does not compile today, so advertising it as supported was a promise the tree contradicts. Found by auditing every supported epoch's export list against the live surface, not by a failing example -- this epoch's example happened not to use either name.
dropped.7: Additive only: RunRecord gained one OPTIONAL field, codeVersion, so a walk can say whether the code changed under an in-flight run rather than handing the reader a test. RunRecord reaches this capability's report through RuntimeOptions.journal, and nothing in epoch 7 stops compiling — no caller must set the field and none may be broken by reading it. Dropped rather than retained because a retained epoch-7 template would be byte-identical to the retained epoch-6 one (contracts/compatibility/runtime/v6.ts): that file is frozen, still compiles against these types, and therefore ALREADY holds the property a v7 template would assert. A second near-duplicate starter is the catalogue this directory's own doc warns against.
dropped.8: JournalStore gained a required readStep(runId, key) method, so a host that IMPLEMENTS the interface no longer satisfies it — the whole point of RuntimeOptions.journal being that a deployment with its own database supplies one. The frozen templates only CONSUME a journal, so they still compile; that is the documented gap between classification coverage and compile-time exercise, not evidence the epoch holds. Consumers add the method: it answers ONE settled step by key, undefined when it has not settled, and both shipped databases key the table (run_id, key) so it is an index seek.
dropped.9: JournalStore gained a required readSleeps(runId) method, so a host that IMPLEMENTS the interface no longer satisfies it — the whole point of RuntimeOptions.journal being that a deployment with its own database supplies one. The frozen templates only CONSUME a journal, so they still compile; that is the documented gap between classification coverage and compile-time exercise, not evidence the epoch holds. Consumers add the method: it answers EVERY durable wait of a run, ordered by key, as SleepEntry (a SleepRecord plus its key), and both shipped databases key the sleeps table (run_id, key) so it is a range scan already in that order. It is what stops a replay re-claiming every elapsed sleep it walks past — measured in production at 2,675 journal POSTs on one run, rising +1 per delivery across 69 deliveries.
dropped.10: Renamed for naming consistency (API naming review): same as epoch 6 -- promises decliningRuntime and SkipGreeting, both removed. Every runtime epoch from 1 to 11 carries a character-identical export list, so the rename invalidated all of them at once.
dropped.11: Renamed for naming consistency (API naming review): decliningRuntime -> rejectingRuntime, pairing with the existing rejectingWorkflows, and SkipGreeting -> SkipGreetingOption, a boolean-or-thunk union named as a verb.

dropped.1: UploadStore gained a required `open(id)`: the byte route reads one window per chunk and every one of them resolved the record for itself, so a range download cost a look-up per megabyte.
